description: Just trying to make the best website possible and win
summary:
I developed Skyblink, a platform that makes learning about space more accessible and engaging. This is a great space for beginners and experienced astronomers alike to access the findings of SPHEREx.
Skyblink addresses the challenge of making complex scientific information easier to understand and navigate. I wanted to create an experience that welcomes people regardless of their background knowledge.
This project matters because learning about the universe shouldn’t require a scientific background. By making space more approachable, I hope to spark curiosity, encourage learning, and inspire more people to take an interest in scientific discovery and the wonder that is our universe.
details:
I created Skyblink because I wanted to give all this wonderful space data a face. There’s so much to explore, but technical files and complicated tools make it hard to know where to start and what you're even looking at. I wanted to turn that experience into something visual where people could follow their curiosity without needing a background in astronomy or antiquated archives.

Skyblink lets users search for an object or choose a spot in the sky, then watch how it changes across NASA’s SPHEREx observations. It lines up the images so that they’re easier to compare, and a “Changes” view helps highlight movement and differences in brightness. Users can also explore brightness over time, download data, and save or share what they find which I feel is the most important part of research.

I used HTML and Cloudflare to build the experience and connect it to public astronomy data. The creative part was bringing those observations together in a way that feels interactive rather than overwhelming. Instead of just looking at a single space image, users can replay observations and investigate what catches their attention and look at the bigger picture through small pieces.

Working on my own, I focused on simplicity, accessibility, and clear explanations. I also made sure the simulated demo was labeled and included information about the data’s current limitations. At the end of the day, I hope Skyblink helps students, educators, researchers and really anyone curious about space in general, feel, that scientific exploration is something they can take part in and love.
